title: The 2017 LCO K2-22 data cannot identify a colour slope when each orbit has a free dust amplitude
abstract: We test whether the 2017 LCO observations of K2-22 can identify a common dust colour slope when dust amount can change each orbit. Seven g visits and 17 i visits have no shared orbit. For a positive colour response multiplied by a free orbit amplitude, a change in colour can be cancelled exactly by a change in amplitude. All predicted fluxes then stay equal. A numerical check leaves a profile score range below 1e-15 and flux differences below 2e-18. Two simultaneous narrow-band pairs pass the main coverage rules. Their conditional 95 percent depth-difference ranges are -10.77 to +4.16 and -16.96 to +0.10 parts per thousand. A small difference from a box template does not persist across the other fits. Thus these tests establish no stable colour signal or new planet. The result formalizes a schedule limitation already noted in the source paper. It applies to the stated separable model and does not exclude colour-dependent shapes or a physical law that links dust amounts across orbits. Code, proof, aggregate results, a figure and external-data retrieval steps support reproduction.

display.caption: LCO colour scores are flat when each orbit has a free amplitude. Two simultaneous colour pairs give broad conditional ranges. The right score is sensitive to the assumed transit shape and baseline. The 3.84 line is a reference score, not a calibrated confidence limit.
